newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Turkey sign anti-terrorism pact.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Turkey sign anti-terrorism pact.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller pledged in talks in Moscow on Wednesday to work together to combat terrorism.

After signing the anti-terrorism agreement, Primakov told a news conference he was satisfied with Turkey's position towards Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya, previously a sore point between the two countries.
"We stated that we stand for settling this problem within the framework of Russia's territorial integrity and that we consider this to be Russia's internal matter," he said.
Turkey has close historical ties with the Caucasus and many Turks were upset by Russia's 21-month military campaign aimed at crushing Chechnya's independence bid.
Moscow is now pulling its troops out of the region under a peace deal with the rebels.
Primakov and Ciller said they had also discussed NATO's plan to expand the alliance, of which Turkey is a member, into eastern Europe.
"We are unanimous that it is necessary to leave Europe without lines of division," Primakov said.
Ciller said: "During our talks I have come to realise how sensitive Russia's position on NATO enlargement is... We (NATO) have never wanted enlargement to pose a threat to Russia."
Russia has long opposed NATO plans to take in former communist countries in central and eastern Europe.
During her two-day visit to Moscow, Ciller also discussed cooperation on gas supplies from Russia to Turkey and bilateral trade, officials said.

Trade between Turkey and Russia will total four billion dollars in 1996, up 14 percent from the year before, Itar-Tass quoted Russia's Deputy Minister of Economic Relations Vladimir Karastin as saying.
Ciller, who is also Turkish deputy prime minister, earlier met Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Moscow's Mayor Yury Luzhkov.
